paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Ἑνώχ, διὰ τί ἐπερωτᾷς καὶ διὰ τί θαυμάζεις περὶ τῆς εὐωδίας τοῦ δένδρου τούτου, καὶ διὰ τί τὸ ἀληθὲς ἐθέλεις γνῶναι;
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen moi; Henōch, dia ti eperōtas kai dia ti thaumazeis peri tēs euōdias tou dendrou toutou, kai dia ti to alēthes etheleis gnōnai?

i18n.en: And he said to me: Enoch, why do you ask, and why do you wonder at the fragrance of this tree, and why do you wish to know the truth?

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἀπεκρίθην αὐτῷ ἐγὼ Ἑνώχ, λέγων· Περὶ πάντων εἰδέναι θέλω, μάλιστα δὲ περὶ τοῦ δένδρου τούτου.
paragraphs.translit: Tote apekrithēn autō egō Henōch, legōn; Peri pantōn eidenai thelō, malista de peri tou dendrou toutou.

i18n.en: Then I, Enoch, answered him, saying: I wish to know about all things, but most of all about this tree.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη μοι λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ὄρος τὸ ὑψηλόν, οὗ ἡ κορυφὴ ὁμοία θρόνῳ θεοῦ, καθέδρα ἐστὶν οὗ καθέσει ὁ ἅγιος καὶ μέγας, ὁ κύριος τῆς δόξης, ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῦ αἰῶνος, ὅταν κατέλθῃ ἐπισκέψασθαι τὴν γῆν μετ' ἀγαθοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai apekrithē moi legōn; Touto to oros to hypsēlon, hou hē koryphē homoia thronō theou, kathedra estin hou kathesei ho hagios kai megas, ho kyrios tēs doxēs, ho basileus tou aiōnos, hotan katelthē episkepsasthai tēn gēn met' agathou.

i18n.en: And he answered me, saying: This high mountain, whose summit is like the throne of God, is the seat where the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the eternal King, shall sit, when he descends to visit the earth with goodness.

paragraphs.commentary: 'When he will descend to visit the earth in goodness' — the eschatological-descent framework that the Hebrew Bible Sinai-theophany tradition (Ex 19 + Deut 33:2) supplies as the source-material. The throne-of-glory mountain is the cosmic-axis-mundi from which the cosmic-judgement-descent will be made. *the great Lord, the Holy One* is the divine-circumlocution-title convention — see overlay `holy-great-one-great-glory-divine-circumlocution-titles-convention`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ τοῦτο τὸ δένδρον εὐωδίας, οὐδεμία σὰρξ ἐξουσίαν ἔχει τοῦ ἅψασθαι, μέχρι τῆς μεγάλης κρίσεως, ἐν ᾗ ἐκδίκησις πάντων καὶ τελείωσις μέχρι αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Kai touto to dendron euōdias, oudemia sarx exousian echei tou hapsasthai, mechri tēs megalēs kriseōs, en hē ekdikēsis pantōn kai teleiōsis mechri aiōnos.

i18n.en: And this fragrant tree — no flesh has authority to touch it, until the great judgment, in which there shall be vengeance upon all and consummation forever.

paragraphs.commentary: **The tree of life shall be transplanted to the holy place by the temple of the Lord, the Eternal King.** The eschatological-restoration: the tree-of-life is reserved for the righteous at the great judgement; afterward it is transplanted to the cosmographic-center. The framework is inherited by Rev 22:2, 22:14 (the tree of life in the new Jerusalem); the Rev 22 → 1 En 25 dependency is foundational (Bauckham 1993 *Climax of Prophecy* 310-321).

paragraphs.text: Τότε δικαίοις καὶ ὁσίοις δοθήσεται· ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς εἰς ζωήν, καὶ μεταφυτευθήσεται εἰς τόπον ἅγιον, παρὰ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ βασιλέως τοῦ αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Tote dikaiois kai hosiois dothēsetai; ho karpos autou tois eklektois eis zōēn, kai metaphyteuthēsetai eis topon hagion, para ton oikon tou theou, tou basileōs tou aiōnos.

i18n.en: Then it shall be given to the righteous and the holy: its fruit for the elect, unto life; and it shall be transplanted to a holy place, beside the house of God, the eternal King.

paragraphs.text: Τότε εὐφρανθήσονται εὐφραινόμενοι καὶ χαρήσονται, καὶ εἰς τὸν ναὸν εἰσελεύσονται· καὶ ὀσμὴ αὐτοῦ ἔσται ἐν τοῖς ὀστέοις αὐτῶν, καὶ ζωὴν ζήσονται μακρὰν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὁποίαν ἔζησαν οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν λύπη καὶ μάστιξ καὶ βάσανος καὶ πληγὴ οὐχ ἅψεται αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Tote euphranthēsontai euphrainomenoi kai charēsontai, kai eis ton naon eiseleusontai; kai osmē autou estai en tois osteois autōn, kai zōēn zēsontai makran epi tēs gēs, hopoian ezēsan hoi pateres autōn, kai en tais hēmerais autōn lypē kai mastix kai basanos kai plēgē ouch hapsetai autōn.

i18n.en: Then they shall rejoice with joy and be glad, and they shall enter the holy place; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as their fathers lived, and in their days no sorrow nor scourge nor torment nor plague shall touch them.

paragraphs.text: Τότε εὐλόγησα τὸν κύριον τῆς δόξης τὸν βασιλέα τοῦ αἰῶνος, ὅτι ἡτοίμασεν τὰ τοιαῦτα ἀνθρώποις δικαίοις, καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἔκτισεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς δοθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: Tote eulogēsa ton kyrion tēs doxēs ton basilea tou aiōnos, hoti hētoimasen ta toiauta anthrōpois dikaiois, kai ta toiauta ektisen kai eipen autois dothēnai.

i18n.en: Then I blessed the Lord of glory, the eternal King, because he had prepared such things for righteous people, and had created such things, and had said that they should be given to them.
